rows.title: UCHealth’s merger with a 100-year-old Pueblo hospital strengthens its dominant spot in the health care market
rows.standfirst: The merger with Parkview Health System, finalized in December, is the latest in a trend of hospital consolidations across the country

rows.title: Denver moved 277 migrants from an encampment into shelter — as 443 more arrived
rows.standfirst: Denver took several busloads of migrants from an encampment to three shelters, but some were left begging for spots.

rows.title: What’s Working: San Luis Valley attracts young artists looking for a more affordable, creative Colorado
rows.standfirst: One of the more challenging places to make a living in Colorado is in the San Luis Valley. While relatively affordable, this southern rural region is also among the poorest, with Costilla, Alamosa and Saguache among counties in the state with the highest poverty rates. Perhaps that’s why young artists are attracted to the area. […]

rows.title: Colorado has given more than $2.3 million in federal pandemic aid to people in debt to their HOAs
rows.standfirst: At least 13 homeowners received more than $20,000 under the Colorado Emergency Mortgage Assistance Program to settle their HOA debt. One received nearly $60,000.

rows.title: Only a nuclear reactor can make Pueblo “whole” after Xcel Energy closes last coal-fired plant, local group says
rows.standfirst: After a 10-month study, a community-based committee says the only energy technology that can make up for lost jobs, taxes and economic activity is an advanced nuclear power plant

rows.title: Colorado rivers may shrink by 30% as climate change continues, report says
rows.standfirst: 2024 update to Colorado State University’s comprehensive climate study projects depleted rivers, shaky snowpack, more wildfire risk and a Front Range baking under ozone pollution

rows.title: Colorado property manager settles for $1 million after investigation finds it illegally billed residents
rows.standfirst: Four Star Realty, which mostly rents to college students, illegally charged for routine repairs and other services

rows.title: Granby Ranch owners ban elected officials, homeowners from accessing amenities, restaurants and “sidewalks, patios and lawns”
rows.standfirst: Letters from the law firm representing developers Bob and David Glarner ban members of the Granby Ranch Metro District board — and their spouses — from the ski area, golf course, trails and facilities

rows.title: Colorado’s Eastern Plains prepare to protect people and livestock as wind chills predicted at minus 30
rows.standfirst: Rural lawmakers, meanwhile, accuse Gov. Polis of ignoring them as they brace for freezing temps and blowing snow

rows.title: In southwestern Colorado, another publication succumbs to economics and prints its final edition
rows.standfirst: The monthly Four Corners Free Press celebrated its 20th anniversary in September. But printing costs and dwindling advertising hastened its demise.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s arts budget hasn’t budged in 10 years. This year, it could more than double.
rows.standfirst: Even Utah’s got us beat. Gov. Polis proposed a one-time extra $3 million infusion to get arts above $5 million. Plus: Art, entertainment and news organizations unionize, more!

rows.title: After “Snowpocalypse” killed their power, Silverton is turning on microgrids
rows.standfirst: San Miguel Power sees community-sized solar grids as a way for small mountain towns to keep the lights burning through storms and avalanches

rows.title: Denver receives record number of applications from landlords looking for new rental licenses
rows.standfirst: The Department of Excise and Licenses received more than 5,000 applications in December from landlords looking to comply with new safety standards

rows.title: “We don’t want to be activists”: The farmers pushing for stronger pipeline safety rules
rows.standfirst: Colorado utilities regulators Wednesday will begin work on rules to improve safety inspections of pipelines like the one that leaked gas and destroyed Mark and Julie Nygren’s home

rows.title: Colorado offered $1.45 billion in incentives to attract new business. About 5% was claimed.
rows.standfirst: That’s still about $66.3 million. In return, companies have created about 20,000 jobs — at least as far as state officials know.

rows.title: PHOTOS: Bill Pickett Rodeo celebrates 40 years of riding, roping and mutton bustin’ at the National Western
rows.standfirst: The 40th annual MLK, Jr. African American Heritage Rodeo of Champions drew top Black cowboys and cowgirls and a lot of little wranglers with big-arena aspirations

rows.title: 10 years after the last uranium speculator left Cañon City, an Australian company is on the hunt
rows.standfirst: Interest in cleaner electricity generation and war in Ukraine has resparked interest in proven uranium deposits in Fremont and Moffat counties.

rows.title: Rural Colorado awarded $113.5 million to build better broadband, but most applicants left empty-handed
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Broadband Office hopes additional federal funds, like the upcoming $826.5 million BEAD allocation, will take care of the rest.

rows.title: Douglas County sues to overturn state board’s decision to block property tax relief plan
rows.standfirst: The 15-page lawsuit brought against the State Board of Equalization argues the board both didn’t have the authority to block the tax break and that it didn’t follow Colorado’s open meetings laws in doing so

rows.title: Watch: The Colorado Sun talks the High Cost of Colorado housing
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun reporters Jennifer Brown and Michael Booth spoke with speakers about the high cost of housing, evictions, affordable housing, rent control and more during its High Cost of Colorado event.

rows.title: Colorado mountain town real estate settles from pandemic frenzy with a big drop in deals, but prices remain record-high
rows.standfirst: Mountain communities saw a 20% to 30% decrease in real estate sales volume and transactions in 2023 but prices have not dropped as the number of homes for sale reached record lows

rows.title: Colorado doubles penalties for leaking pipelines, but regulators left open a reporting loophole
rows.standfirst: The Public Utilities Commission adopted rules requiring operators of natural gas pipelines to disclose more data on leaks and the location of their lines “to the extent available”

rows.title: Colorado pledges to play nice as Nebraska plows ahead on $628M canal at the state line
rows.standfirst: Though details remain sparse on the new South Platte River project, local water users say, for now, the cornhuskers are entitled to their fair share of the river

rows.title: Nearly 90% of people who are homeless in Denver were already living in Colorado, report shows
rows.standfirst: The annual State of Homelessness Report is based on data collected by agencies in 7 metro counties and shows most people who are unhoused lost shelter when a relationship ended or they lost a job

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado added just 300 jobs in December, as unemployment rate rose to 3.4%
rows.standfirst: Don’t look at Colorado’s latest jobs report unless you want to be depressed, but know it may only be for a few months. The December numbers, released Friday, have the state’s unemployment rate on the rise, to 3.4%. Employers added just 300 jobs last month. In the same report, November data was revised downward. Nonfarm […]

rows.title: Replacement ranch needed for storied Colorado family. 86,000 acres or best offer.
rows.standfirst: After the state moved on from a 25-year lease at Chico Basin Ranch, the Phillips family needs land and moving vans for 1,500 cattle.

rows.title: On a dead-end street in north Denver, migrants are surviving winter with the help of an army of volunteers
rows.standfirst: As the city reinstates time limits on hotel stays, volunteers are making plans to help hundreds more migrants in camps

rows.title: How hard is it for rural Colorado hospitals to hire CEOs? Ask the 24-year-old boss at the medical center in Julesburg.
rows.standfirst: Turnover among top managers of critical access hospitals in Colorado is double that of the nation. It’s a tough job, some say, even in cities with plenty of resources and mentors.

rows.title: Denver mayor says goal to shelter 1,000 people was achieved, plans to provide shelter for 1,000 more in 2024
rows.standfirst: People sheltered in 2023 will be quickly directed to more traditional housing units, many in complexes where help with health, employment counseling is available

rows.title: Gig workers are employees, Denver auditor says as city seeks more than $1 million in penalties
rows.standfirst: Instawork and Gigpro allegedly misclassified more than 3,000 people as independent contractors

rows.title: Young Colorado renters need to choose if they’ll pay the landlord, the hospital or grandma
rows.standfirst: A tenant who earns minimum wage would have to work 77 hours per week to afford a one-bedroom apartment at fair market rent

rows.title: Colorado pastor accused of defrauding investors of $3M via cryptocurrency scheme says he got help from “the Lord”
rows.standfirst: Authorities say Eli Regalado of Denver and his wife targeted Christian community and told followers that God would make them rich

rows.title: Governor removes Democrat from board that blocked Douglas County’s property tax cut, replaces him with Republican
rows.standfirst: Jared Polis took Bernie Buescher off the State Board of Equalization, giving Republicans a majority on the panel that reviews local property tax decisions

rows.title: Colorado plans to offer tax credits, loan guarantees to quantum-technology startups and expanding companies
rows.standfirst: A bill soon to be introduced in the legislature would mark the first time the state is providing a loan guarantee as a business incentive. The proposal is contingent on more federal funding for the new form of computing.

rows.title: At a Glenwood Springs mobile home park, residents are working toward controlling their destiny
rows.standfirst: To avoid a large corporation swooping in, 3-Mile residents decided they needed to purchase the park themselves

But you may not know it from national data released earlier this week. rows.title: Tent meant for festivals and galas used to put services for Grand Junction’s homeless under one roof
rows.standfirst: The one-stop-shop for help has riled some neighbors, but the city says the pavilion is a bridge to a permanent Resource Center

rows.title: Colorado and Wyoming get $15 million to launch “engine” for profitable climate change solutions
rows.standfirst: National Science Foundation offers up to $160 million over 10 years to translate startup ideas into big-scale greenhouse gas fixes

rows.title: Denver Art Museum workers will vote on a union in March. Here are the details.
rows.standfirst: If the union succeeds, it would represent about 250 workers in more than 60 jobs throughout the museum

rows.title: Colorado Democrats launch second attempt to allow more accessory dwelling units to ease housing crisis
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1152 is the first of several marquee bills Democrats are expected to introduce this year that would target city and county land-use regulations to tackle Colorado’s affordable housing crisis

rows.title: Colorado had money to stop an extra 1,500 evictions in 2023. The Polis administration told renters not to apply.
rows.standfirst: As state officials were limiting applications for rental assistance, Colorado lawmakers in March 2023 approved $8 million in additional help. The money was never spent.
